articles.excerpt: En 2025, le patrimoine en ressources naturelles du Canada, c'est-à-dire la valeur en dollars de certaines réserves de ressources naturelles, s'est chiffré à 1 234 milliards de dollars, en baisse de 7 % par rapport à 1 334 milliards de dollars en 2024. Les ressources énergétiques, les ressources minérales et le bois représentaient environ 7 % du patrimoine national du Canada en 2025, selon les données figurant dans les comptes du bilan national pour le quatrième trimestre de 2025. Les ressources énergétiques représentaient près de la moitié (47 %) de la valeur totale de l'ensemble des actifs en ressources naturelles en 2025. Venaient ensuite les ressources minérales (39 %) et le bois (14 %).
articles.summary: En 2025, le patrimoine en ressources naturelles du Canada, soit la valeur des réserves de ressources naturelles, s'élève à 1 234 milliards de dollars, en baisse de 7 % par rapport à 1 334 milliards en 2024. Les ressources énergétiques représentent 47 % de cette valeur, les ressources minérales 39 % et le bois 14 %. Ces actifs forment environ 7 % du patrimoine national, selon les comptes du bilan national du quatrième trimestre de 2025.

articles.excerpt: Token fraud is here and it’s BAD (YouTube) Claire Vo runs ChatPRD , an AI platform that helps product managers "turn an idea into a spec". The product has been live since the GPT-4 era, and Claire has been building it in public for much of that time. In this YouTube video (see also the accompanying Twitter post ) Claire describes the flood of token fraud she has seen from groups abusing the product's free trial, sometimes just to get free AI usage but often to resell tokens or run other commercial enterprises on top of the ChatPRD agent. I am funding a international Roblox and Fortnite map studio. They run a loop of free trials and promo codes and then tunnel to my agent and use it to build Roblox and Fortnite maps. Apparently one of the common prompts Claire saw running through her agent involved SVGs of pelicans riding bicycles! Presumably the token scammers are using that to help sniff the underlying models - different model families have a definite signature, and I've used it like this in the past to try and guess the identity of stealth preview models on platforms like OpenRouter. Claire is winding down her free trials entirely, which sadly looks like the right decision in the face of this abuse. Tags: youtube , ai , generative-ai , llms , pelican-riding-a-bicycle , ai-misuse
articles.summary: Claire Vo, fondatrice de ChatPRD, une plateforme d'IA d'aide aux chefs de produit, décrit dans une vidéo YouTube la vague de fraude sur les jetons qui exploite son essai gratuit, souvent pour revendre des jetons ou faire tourner d'autres activités commerciales via l'agent. Elle met fin à ses essais gratuits, ce que l'auteur juge être la bonne décision face à ces abus. L'auteur souligne aussi que des requêtes de type « pélicans à vélo en SVG » pourraient servir à identifier les modèles sous-jacents.

articles.excerpt: PostgreSQL 19 Released Most years PostgreSQL ships a new release in September, but this year's release came two months later thanks mainly to the flurry of issues that the PostgreSQL team needed to address as part of the ongoing AI-reported vulnerability apocalypse. This release was definitely worth the wait. My favorite new feature is this one: For applications that send reads to standbys, PostgreSQL 19 adds "read-your-writes" consistency with the new WAIT FOR LSN command. A session on a standby can use WAIT FOR LSN to wait until the standby has replayed the write-ahead log (WAL) up to a specific log sequence number (LSN) before running a query, so the application can read data it just wrote on the primary. In practice, that looks like this: UPDATE movie SET genre = 'Dramatic' WHERE genre = 'Drama'; SELECT pg_current_wal_insert_lsn(); That returns a value like 0/0306EE20 . Store that somewhere (a signed cookie would work) such that on a subsequent request your application can do: WAIT FOR LSN '0/0306EE20' WITH (TIMEOUT '0.1s'); SELECT * FROM movie WHERE genre = 'Drama'; The timeout is optional - if you provide one you'll get an error if the replica you are talking to doesn't catch up within the specified time. I first encountered this pattern in Wikipedia , which has a hand-rolled version of this built against MySQL replication: In addition to this, MediaWiki attempts to ensure that the user sees events occurring on the wiki in chronological order. A few seconds of lag can…
articles.summary: PostgreSQL 19 est sorti avec deux mois de retard, en partie à cause de nombreux correctifs de vulnérabilités signalées grâce à l'IA. La nouveauté phare est la commande WAIT FOR LSN, qui permet à une session sur un réplica d'attendre que le WAL soit rejoué jusqu'à un LSN donné, afin de lire ses propres écritures faites sur le serveur principal (cohérence « read-your-writes »).
articles.title: PostgreSQL 19 Released

articles.excerpt: AWS CloudFormation StackSets now supports custom execution roles for service-managed stack sets, which enables you to scope the permissions StackSets uses in each target AWS account. StackSets deploys the same infrastructure, such as networking and security settings, across thousands of accounts and Regions in one operation. With a custom execution role, you can also use nested stacks, macros, and transforms in service-managed stack sets, which allows you to deploy the reusable templates you use for individual stacks across your organization. With a custom execution role, you define what StackSets can do in each account. By default, service-managed stack sets use a role in each account that can provision any resource in a template without additional setup, and that default remains available. Now, you can provide a template that defines an IAM role, called the execution role, and StackSets creates it in each account before deploying. For example, a stack set that creates Amazon S3 buckets can use an execution role limited to CloudFormation and Amazon S3 permissions. When you update the execution role template, StackSets updates the role in every account it deployed to. To get started, choose Set execution role when you create a stack set in the CloudFormation console, or use the AWS CLI or AWS SDKs. To learn more, visit the documentation and the AWS DevOps Blog . articles.excerpt: Amazon Cognito now supports OAuth client ID metadata documents (CIMD). Amazon Cognito helps you implement secure sign-in and access control for users, AI agents, and microservices in minutes. With CIMD, Model Context Protocol (MCP) clients and AI agents can sign users in to your user pool without registering a separate app client. Previously, each external client needed its own app client, either created in advance or through dynamic client registration, and you had to manage and clean up those clients over time. With CIMD, a client uses an HTTPS URL as its client ID and publishes a JSON metadata document at that URL. When the client starts sign-in, Cognito fetches and validates the document and uses it to identify the client and validate its sign-in request. You decide which clients to accept with CIMD policies that map URL patterns to one of your app clients, and Cognito grants only the scopes and grant types that both the app client and the metadata document allow. For example, a company that runs an MCP server can accept an AI assistant by allowing the URL where that assistant publishes its metadata without creating or maintaining an app client for it. CIMD is available on the Essentials and Plus feature plans in all AWS Regions where Amazon Cognito is available. To learn more, see Client ID metadata documents (CIMD) in the Amazon Cognito Developer Guide.
articles.summary: Amazon Cognito prend désormais en charge les documents de métadonnées d'identifiant client OAuth (CIMD). Un client, comme un client MCP ou un agent IA, utilise une URL HTTPS comme identifiant et publie un document JSON de métadonnées, ce qui lui permet de se connecter sans qu'une application cliente distincte soit créée pour lui. Les politiques CIMD déterminent quels clients sont acceptés, et la fonctionnalité est offerte dans les forfaits Essentials et Plus dans toutes les régions où Cognito est disponible.
articles.title: Amazon Cognito now supports client ID metadata documents

articles.excerpt: With upgrades to its storage layer, Amazon Aurora DSQL now delivers up to 50% higher write throughput for many transactional workloads. Data loads finish sooner, and tables whose primary key always increases, such as tables keyed by a timestamp, an identity column, or a time-ordered ID like ULID or UUIDv7, see even greater benefits. Applications such as audit logs, ledgers, and event feeds are read in time order, and keying them by time keeps those reads fast. You can now use that design for write-heavy tables too. In our tests, an audit log table keyed by event time accepted up to 200% more inserts per second. The improvement is available in all AWS Regions where Aurora DSQL is available, for new and existing clusters, at no additional cost. To learn more, see the Aurora DSQL User Guide .
articles.summary: Amazon Aurora DSQL annonce jusqu'à 50 % de débit d'écriture en plus pour de nombreuses charges transactionnelles, grâce à des améliorations de sa couche de stockage. Les tables dont la clé primaire croît toujours, comme celles indexées par horodatage ou par identifiant ordonné dans le temps (ULID, UUIDv7), en tirent un bénéfice encore plus grand ; dans les tests d'AWS, une table de journal d'audit a accepté jusqu'à 200 % d'insertions de plus par seconde. La mise à niveau est offerte sans frais supplémentaires dans toutes les régions où Aurora DSQL est disponible, pour les clusters nouveaux et existants.
articles.title: Amazon Aurora DSQL now delivers up to 50% higher write throughput

articles.excerpt: Amazon CloudFront now allows web development and SaaS platforms to serve different tiers of customers on the same wildcard domain by using IP addresses to route them to the right configuration. For example, these platforms can serve premium and pro customers from dedicated Anycast static IP address lists, each with its own configuration, and serve free-tier customers on the shared CloudFront IP addresses, all under *. example.com . Additionally, these customers also have visibility into viewer connections with connection logging. Previously, CloudFront chose the configuration from the domain name alone, so the same domain always went to the same configuration. With address-based selection, you can register the same wildcard domain on several IP lists and send each list to its own tenant. Because you control which clients resolve to which IP list, you can shift traffic between your service tiers without your customers needing to make any changes. You can also serve IoT devices, embedded SDKs, and older TLS clients that connect by IP address without sending a domain name in the TLS handshake (Server Name Indication, or SNI). With viewer fallback, you choose a distribution to accept these connections, and CloudFront uses the Host header in each request to serve the right content. Connection logs now also record HTTPS connections to these tenants which helps you troubleshoot how clients connect. These features are available at all CloudFront edge locations. To learn more, see…
articles.summary: Amazon CloudFront permet désormais aux plateformes SaaS et de développement web de servir différents niveaux de clients sur un même domaine générique, en routant le trafic selon l'adresse IP (listes d'adresses Anycast statiques dédiées). Des fonctionnalités de repli pour les connexions sans SNI et de journalisation des connexions complètent cette mise à jour, disponible à tous les emplacements périphériques.
articles.title: Amazon CloudFront adds IP based routing and connection logs to SaaS Manager

articles.excerpt: Amazon CloudFront now lets web development platforms and SaaS providers move a customer's domain to their platform in a single request with no downtime, and serve requests to the domain while the TLS certificate is being configured. The CloudFront multi-tenant distributions allow these platforms to serve many customer domains from one shared configuration. Together, these features help move existing AWS customers to multi-tenant distributions without impacting their traffic. Previously, moving a domain that was already in use required disabling the original distribution, using a wildcard workaround, or contacting AWS Support. Now you can bring customer domains onto your multi-tenant setup as part of creating or updating a tenant. With the new OnDomainTakeover option, CloudFront checks domain ownership through DNS records and then moves one or more domains in a single request. This works within an AWS account or across accounts. If you add a domain before its certificate is issued, CloudFront serves it over HTTP until you attach a certificate. That gives you time to validate the domain with AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) or another certificate authority and attach the certificate once it's issued. These features are available in all edge locations at no additional cost. To learn more, see Move domains and Domains without a certificate in the Amazon CloudFront Developer Guide.
articles.summary: Amazon CloudFront permet désormais aux plateformes SaaS et de développement web de migrer le domaine d'un client vers leur plateforme en une seule requête, sans interruption de service, et de servir le domaine pendant la configuration du certificat TLS. Une option OnDomainTakeover vérifie la propriété des domaines par DNS et peut déplacer plusieurs domaines à la fois, au sein d'un même compte AWS ou entre comptes. Ces fonctionnalités sont offertes sans frais supplémentaires dans tous les emplacements périphériques.
articles.title: Amazon CloudFront simplifies domain moves and onboarding for SaaS Manager

articles.excerpt: Amazon Connect Customer announces the general availability of Resolutions, an agentic operations solution that resolves high-volume work end-to-end, including refund requests, transaction disputes, fraud investigations, and insurance claims. Resolutions helps businesses reduce resolution times and cost to serve by combining the reasoning of AI agents with the reliability of deterministic workflows. Every request follows business policy, gets the oversight it requires, and ends in a verifiable outcome. Managers describe a process in natural language or upload standard operating procedures (SOPs), and Resolutions generates a Work plan in minutes. As it builds the Work plan, Resolutions asks clarifying questions that surface exceptions, set decision rules, and define approval thresholds, closing the gaps an SOP leaves open. Resolutions then opens a Resolutions Case for each incoming request and applies the right Work plan. AI agents gather information, apply policy, act across your business applications, and ask customers for missing details to drive every Case to completion. Each Step can run on prebuilt AI agents, AI agents configured in Amazon Connect Customer, or your own, while human specialists handle approvals and exceptions with the context they need to act. For example, a bank resolving a transaction dispute can have AI agents pull the transaction history, check the claim against chargeback rules, email the cardholder for a missing receipt, and issue a provisional…
articles.summary: Amazon Connect annonce la disponibilité générale de Resolutions, une solution agentique qui traite de bout en bout les demandes à fort volume, comme les remboursements, les litiges de transactions, les enquêtes de fraude et les réclamations d'assurance. Elle combine le raisonnement d'agents IA et des workflows déterministes, les gestionnaires pouvant décrire un processus en langage naturel ou téléverser leurs procédures opérationnelles standards pour générer un plan de travail.
articles.title: Amazon Connect launches Resolutions, an agentic solution for high-volume operational work

articles.excerpt: AWS Lambda announces OpenTelemetry (OTel) support for Lambda durable functions. You can now trace your durable executions and emit traces to Amazon CloudWatch and other industry-standard observability tools. This helps you find bottlenecks in your system, root cause failures faster, and understand how your workflows behave in production. With Lambda durable functions, you can build resilient, multi-step applications and AI workflows that run for up to one year, with built-in checkpointing and automatic retries. Durable functions can run for hours, or days, suspending and resuming across many Lambda invocations. The new OpenTelemetry plugin emits a unified trace that spans a full durable execution, including steps, waits, callbacks, and chained function invocations. You can use the trace to gain operational insights across your executions including step durations, retries, and failures across executions. The OpenTelemetry plugin is available for the TypeScript, Python, and Java SDKs. You can enable OpenTelemetry support by adding the OpenTelemetry plugin package alongside the Durable Execution SDK and register it on your durable handler or using an environment variable. OpenTelemetry support for Lambda durable functions is available in all AWS Regions that support Lambda durable functions. To get started, see the OpenTelemetry plugin documentation , the plugin interface documentation , and the sample application . To learn more, read the blog post .
articles.summary: AWS annonce la prise en charge d'OpenTelemetry pour les fonctions durables de Lambda, ce qui permet d'émettre des traces vers Amazon CloudWatch et d'autres outils d'observabilité standards. Une trace unifiée couvre l'ensemble d'une exécution durable, incluant les étapes, les attentes, les callbacks et les invocations de fonctions chaînées, afin d'analyser les durées, les nouvelles tentatives et les échecs. Le plugin est offert pour les SDK TypeScript, Python et Java, dans toutes les régions où les fonctions durables sont disponibles.
articles.title: AWS Lambda durable functions now supports OpenTelemetry tracing

articles.excerpt: You can now assess a seller's security, buy, and deploy supported products in one conversation with AWS Marketplace agent mode, the conversational AI experience for procuring cloud solutions. You share your requirement once, and agent mode applies them as it guides you through discovery, purchase, and deployment. Describe your use case in natural language to get recommended software, services, AI agents and tools, and multi-product solutions that fit your business needs. To assess a seller's security, request documents such as System and Organization Controls (SOC) 2 reports, and get a criterion-by-criterion assessment against a standard cloud security questionnaire, the Consensus Assessments Initiative Questionnaire (CAIQ). When you're ready to buy, sign in with your AWS account. Agent mode explains pricing and terms so you know what you're committing to, shows your organizations' purchase requirements, and completes the purchase after you review the terms and confirm. For supported products, agent mode reviews your AWS environment, proposes a deployment plan with the estimated monthly cost, and deploys after you approve. It then shows you how to start using the product and helps you troubleshoot if a step fails. Agent mode is available in all AWS Regions where AWS Marketplace is available. To get started, open agent mode on the AWS Marketplace website. To learn more, see Agent mode for AWS Marketplace in the AWS Marketplace Buyer Guide.
articles.summary: AWS Marketplace propose désormais un mode agent conversationnel qui permet d'évaluer la sécurité d'un fournisseur, d'acheter puis de déployer des produits pris en charge dans une seule conversation. L'outil recommande logiciels, services et solutions multi-produits à partir d'une description en langage naturel, et fournit une évaluation de sécurité selon le questionnaire CAIQ à partir de rapports SOC 2. Il est disponible dans toutes les régions où AWS Marketplace est offert.
articles.title: AWS Marketplace agent mode now helps you assess, buy, and deploy solutions

articles.excerpt: Amazon WorkSpaces Applications now supports WebAuthn redirection, so users can sign in to websites and applications in their streaming session with a FIDO2 authenticator on their local device, such as a security key, Windows Hello, or Touch ID. Previously, an authenticator attached to the user's computer was not available inside the streaming session, so organizations that require phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication (MFA) had to use weaker sign-in methods or keep those applications off WorkSpaces Applications. This helps organizations with FIDO2 requirements stream those applications. When an application in the session makes a WebAuthn request, WorkSpaces Applications forwards it to the user's device, where the authenticator signs it and returns the response. Private keys never leave the user's device. Administrators turn it on per stack in the console or API, and on Windows fleets can limit it to an allow list of processes. For example, a bank can let employees sign in to Microsoft 365 in their streaming session with the same security key they use on their laptop. WebAuthn redirection is available at no additional charge in all AWS commercial Regions and AWS GovCloud (US) Regions where WorkSpaces Applications is available. To get started, select Enable WebAuthn redirection under User Settings for your stack, use an image with the WorkSpaces Applications agent released on or after October 20, 2026, and connect with the WorkSpaces Applications client for Windows…
articles.summary: Amazon WorkSpaces Applications prend désormais en charge la redirection WebAuthn : les utilisateurs peuvent se connecter à des sites et applications dans leur session de diffusion avec un authentificateur FIDO2 local, comme une clé de sécurité, Windows Hello ou Touch ID, sans que les clés privées quittent leur appareil. La fonctionnalité s'active par pile dans la console ou l'API, sans frais supplémentaires, dans toutes les Régions commerciales AWS et dans les Régions AWS GovCloud (US) où le service est offert.
articles.title: Amazon WorkSpaces Applications now supports WebAuthn redirection

articles.excerpt: Amazon Route 53 now offers Private Endpoint Health Checks, enabling business-critical workloads that never touch the public internet, such as internal APIs, databases, and self-hosted nodes behind internal load balancers or in private subnets, to use native health monitoring and automatic DNS failover. Customers can health-check any reachable private target by IP address, domain, or port over HTTP, HTTPS, or TCP. Customers can associate these health checks with Route 53 DNS records across routing policies in private hosted zones, so Route 53 routes traffic only to healthy endpoints and manages failover automatically. Previously, teams built custom control loops using Amazon CloudWatch alarms, AWS Lambda functions, and the Route 53 API to achieve DNS failover for private resources. With t his approach , failover took several minutes and added operational burden. Detection and DNS failover with Private Endpoint Health Checks are designed to complete in seconds rather than minutes, the service is fully managed, and nothing is exposed to the public internet. The feature supports on-premises and hybrid endpoints reachable from the VPC over AWS Direct Connect or AWS Site-to-Site VPN, enabling resilience patterns such as active-passive disaster recovery and cross-Region DR over AWS Transit Gateway or AWS Cloud WAN. Amazon Route 53 Private Endpoint Health Checks is available today in all AWS commercial regions. To learn more, visit the Amazon Route 53 Developer Guide and the Route…
articles.summary: Amazon Route 53 ajoute des vérifications de santé pour les points de terminaison privés, qui permettent de surveiller des cibles internes (API, bases de données, nœuds derrière des équilibreurs internes) par adresse IP, domaine ou port en HTTP, HTTPS ou TCP. Associées aux enregistrements DNS des zones hébergées privées, elles assurent un basculement automatique vers les points de terminaison sains, en quelques secondes plutôt qu'en minutes, sans exposer les ressources à Internet. La fonctionnalité est offerte dans toutes les régions commerciales AWS et prend en charge les points de terminaison sur site via Direct Connect ou VPN Site-à-Site.
articles.title: Amazon Route 53 now supports health checks for private endpoints

articles.excerpt: Today, AWS announces deal-level revenue attribution for AWS Revenue Measurement (previously Partner Revenue Measurement) capabilities. AWS Partners can now see how the AWS revenue measured for their products maps to specific AWS Marketplace offers and/or APN Customer Engagements (ACE) opportunities. Until now, partners who implemented AWS Revenue Measurement via Resource Tagging , User Agent String or AWS Marketplace Metering could view aggregated, product-level attributed revenue. With this launch, partners can view attributed revenue by offers and opportunities on the Attributed Revenue dashboard in AWS Partner Central for components hosted in partners' own AWS accounts. Two new capabilities make this possible: Revenue Attribution IDs and Marketplace Revenue Share. A Revenue Attribution ID is a unique identifier that allows partners to allocate a product's measured AWS revenue to specific offers and opportunities. Partners create a Revenue Attribution ID, associate it with their deals, and enter a monthly attributed revenue allocation percentage for each deal. Partners with SaaS products on AWS Marketplace can automate allocation to offers with Marketplace Revenue Share. Each month, partners enter the percentage of the product's attributed revenue contributed by AWS Marketplace deals in the Revenue Attribution page, and AWS then calculates the attributed revenue for each active offer. Partners can use Revenue Attribution IDs alongside Marketplace Revenue Share to adjust a…
articles.summary: AWS étend sa mesure des revenus pour les partenaires afin d'attribuer le revenu AWS mesuré de leurs produits à des offres AWS Marketplace et à des opportunités ACE précises, visible dans le tableau de bord Attributed Revenue de AWS Partner Central. Cette attribution repose sur de nouveaux identifiants, les Revenue Attribution IDs, ainsi que sur Marketplace Revenue Share, qui permet d'automatiser la répartition pour les produits SaaS. La fonctionnalité s'applique aux composants hébergés dans les comptes AWS des partenaires.
articles.title: AWS Revenue Measurement now supports deal-level revenue attribution for AWS Marketplace offers and opportunities

articles.excerpt: AWS Lambda now supports a 30-minute function timeout for Event Functions that run on demand, doubling the 15-minute limit for synchronous , asynchronous , and event source mapping (ESM) invocations. On Lambda Managed Instances , synchronous invocations also support up to 30 minutes, while asynchronous and ESM invocations keep the 90-minute timeout launched in September 2026. You can now run long-running workloads such as AI inference, media transcoding, and financial calculations for spiky or steady-state traffic without re-architecting your applications. Customers use Event Functions to build event-driven processors, API backends, and data pipelines. By default, Event Functions run on demand, and Lambda scales them automatically to handle spiky traffic. For steady-state traffic, you can also run them on Lambda Managed Instances, which runs functions on Amazon EC2 instances and maintains the operational simplicity of Lambda. For data-intensive workloads such as AI inference and media processing that run on demand and need longer continuous execution, the 15-minute function timeout had required customers to adopt architectural workarounds. With today's launch, these workloads can run for up to 30 minutes, including when you use Lambda durable functions or invoke your functions from AWS Step Functions Standard workflows . For Event Functions that run on demand, the 30-minute timeout is available in all commercial AWS Regions . On Lambda Managed Instances, it is available for…
articles.summary: AWS Lambda permet désormais un délai d'expiration de 30 minutes pour les fonctions d'événements exécutées à la demande, soit le double de la limite précédente de 15 minutes pour les invocations synchrones, asynchrones et par mappage de source d'événements. Cette limite est disponible dans toutes les Régions AWS commerciales, ce qui permet d'exécuter des charges de travail longues comme l'inférence d'IA ou le transcodage média sans restructurer les applications.
articles.title: AWS Lambda now supports a 30-minute timeout for on-demand Event Functions

articles.excerpt: AWS Transform for migrations now combines migration assessment and migration planning into a single migration job. Previously, you ran separate jobs to build a total cost of ownership (TCO) business case and to plan your migration. With this launch, you upload your on-premises inventory once and use it for both assessment and planning, in any order. After you upload your inventory data, you can estimate your AWS costs and build a business case, group your infrastructure into applications and plan migration waves, or do both. You can rerun either workflow as your data improves. For example, build a business case first and then plan waves from the same inventory, or plan your waves first and then estimate the cost of a single wave. Because assessment and planning share one inventory, your business case and migration plan stay consistent without moving data between jobs. After you finalize your plan and assessment, you can continue in the same job to migrate your networks, deploy landing zones, and migrate servers, storage, and containers. This newest release is available in all AWS Regions where AWS Transform is offered . To learn more about migrating with AWS Transform, visit the product page and documentation .
articles.summary: AWS Transform pour les migrations combine désormais l'évaluation de migration et la planification dans un seul travail de migration. L'inventaire sur site n'est téléversé qu'une fois et peut servir aux deux étapes, dans l'ordre souhaité, ce qui garde le dossier d'affaires et le plan cohérents. Cette version est offerte dans toutes les régions AWS où AWS Transform est disponible.
articles.title: AWS Transform combines migration assessment and planning in one experience

articles.excerpt: AWS Transform now puts applications at the center of every stage of the migration journey, so you can discover, plan, migrate, validate, and track the applications your business runs on rather than just the servers underneath them. Application-level grouping has been part of AWS rehost workflows for years, and AWS Transform now carries that same view through your entire migration. Enterprise migrations typically involve thousands of servers, but the questions that drive decisions are about applications. Using discovery data, AWS Transform identifies application boundaries and dependencies, then surfaces logical groupings of applications, each with its own total cost of ownership (TCO) and migration tracking. AWS Transform also adds built-in surveys, letting application owners validate ownership, system boundaries, and business criticality. A new migration dashboard keeps everyone aligned as the migration moves forward. It gives your team, partners, and leadership one current view of your applications, inventory, assessments, wave plans, and migration status. The dashboard pulls in data from every job in a workspace and updates as work progresses, so no one has to build or maintain separate status reports. You can customize the dashboard and ask questions about migration progress in chat. With a more connected workflow and improved visibility across the migration, AWS Transform lets you move to the cloud with more confidence. This capability is available in all AWS Regions…
articles.summary: AWS Transform étend désormais sa logique centrée sur les applications à toutes les étapes d'une migration : découverte, planification, migration, validation et suivi. Il identifie les frontières et dépendances applicatives à partir des données de découverte, propose un coût total de possession et un suivi de migration par groupe d'applications, et ajoute des sondages intégrés pour faire valider la propriété et la criticité métier. Un nouveau tableau de bord de migration centralise l'état de l'inventaire, des évaluations et des vagues, sans rapports de statut à produire manuellement.
articles.title: AWS Transform extends application-centric migration across the lifecycle

articles.excerpt: The Amazon Interactive Video Service (Amazon IVS) Linux broadcast SDK is now available for IVS Real-Time Streaming. Applications running on Linux can join an IVS stage, receive audio from participants, and send audio back to the stage in real time. The SDK provides a C API and Go language bindings. The Linux broadcast SDK is ideal for AI applications that enrich live streams by processing audio, such as transcription, translation, and content moderation, as well as voice agents that converse with participants. Amazon IVS is a managed live streaming solution designed to make low-latency or real-time video available to viewers around the world. Visit the AWS Region table for a full list of AWS Regions where the Amazon IVS console and APIs for control and creation of video streams are available. To learn more, see IVS Broadcast SDK: Linux Guide .
articles.summary: AWS annonce la disponibilité d'un SDK de diffusion Linux pour Amazon IVS Real-Time Streaming. Il permet aux applications Linux de rejoindre une scène IVS, de recevoir l'audio des participants et de renvoyer de l'audio en temps réel, avec une interface C et des liaisons Go. L'article le présente comme adapté aux applications d'IA qui traitent l'audio (transcription, traduction, modération) et aux agents vocaux.
articles.title: Amazon IVS Real-Time Streaming now provides a Linux broadcast SDK

articles.excerpt: AWS Elemental MediaTailor now supports Dynamic Avail Sizing, which reduces the slate viewers see when ad breaks, also called avails, in live HLS streams go unfilled. MediaTailor is a server-side ad insertion and channel assembly service that personalizes ads in live and on-demand video streams. When the ad decision server returns fewer ads than a break allows, dynamic avail sizing omits the unfilled time and resumes programming early instead of showing slate. To keep playback continuous, MediaTailor holds back a configurable reserve of content behind the live edge and draws on it when a break ends early. When the reserve runs low, MediaTailor requests extra ad time in later breaks to refill it. Free ad-supported streaming TV (FAST) channel operators can use dynamic avail sizing to keep viewers watching programming instead of filler content. Customers turn on dynamic avail sizing for each playback session by adding query parameters to the session initialization URL, with no change to their playback configuration. To learn more, see Dynamic avail sizing in the AWS Elemental MediaTailor User Guide.
articles.summary: AWS Elemental MediaTailor prend désormais en charge le dimensionnement dynamique des pauses publicitaires (Dynamic Avail Sizing) pour les flux HLS en direct. Lorsque le serveur de décision publicitaire retourne moins de publicités que la pause n'en permet, le service retire le temps non comblé et reprend la programmation plus tôt, au lieu d'afficher un écran de remplissage. Il s'active par session via des paramètres de requête ajoutés à l'URL d'initialisation, sans modifier la configuration de lecture.
articles.title: AWS Elemental MediaTailor adds Dynamic Avail Sizing for live HLS

articles.excerpt: Amazon Cognito now integrates with AWS Secrets Manager , so you can store and manage your user pool app client secrets in Secrets Manager. Amazon Cognito helps you implement secure sign-in and access control for users, AI agents, and microservices in minutes. An app client secret authenticates your application to Cognito. Previously, you had to manage and rotate these secrets in Cognito directly. With this integration, you can leverage Secrets Manager for capabilities including rotation, access control with AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies, and encryption with an AWS managed key or your own AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. This can help with periodic credential rotation or compliance requirements; this also helps with keeping secrets out of the console. You can enable this integration for either a new or an existing app client, and disable it at any time. This integration is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon Cognito and AWS Secrets Manager are available, except AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany). Standard AWS Secrets Manager charges apply. To learn more, see the Amazon Cognito Developer Guide for instructions.
articles.summary: Amazon Cognito peut désormais stocker et gérer les secrets de ses clients d'application (app client secrets) dans AWS Secrets Manager, ce qui permet d'utiliser la rotation, le contrôle d'accès IAM et le chiffrement via AWS KMS. Cette intégration peut être activée sur un client existant ou nouveau, et désactivée à tout moment. Elle est offerte dans toutes les régions où Cognito et Secrets Manager sont disponibles, sauf le Cloud souverain européen AWS (Allemagne), avec les frais standards de Secrets Manager.
articles.title: Amazon Cognito now supports AWS Secrets Manager for app client secrets

articles.excerpt: AWS WAF now gives you one place to find and stop unwanted traffic across every application in your account. The new AWS WAF security analytics dashboard brings together traffic from all of your protection packs (web ACLs), whether they protect Regional resources or Amazon CloudFront distributions, into a single view. The dashboard also lets you search request logs right in the console, with no logging pipeline to build, and includes 21 days of full-fidelity request data at no additional cost. It is available alongside the existing dashboard for each protection pack (WebACL), which continues to work as it does today. Until now, spotting a trend across your applications, such as a bot campaign hitting several endpoints or a spike in blocked requests, meant opening each web ACL in turn or individually querying AWS WAF logs. With the AWS WAF security analytics dashboard, you can analyze traffic data from every protection pack (WebACL) at once. You can filter and group traffic by dimensions such as client IP address, country, ASN, user agent, JA4 fingerprint, host, path, rule triggered, and labels. You can see which endpoints are affected and how traffic is changing across all of them. The data is full-fidelity rather than sampled, and filters apply across the whole dashboard. Investigating individual requests has also required delivering AWS WAF logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs, Amazon S3, or Amazon Data Firehose and writing queries. AWS WAF Security analytics dashboard includes…
articles.summary: AWS WAF ajoute un tableau de bord d'analyse de sécurité qui regroupe le trafic de toutes les ACL web du compte, qu'elles protègent des ressources régionales ou des distributions CloudFront. Il permet de filtrer et de grouper le trafic par adresse IP, pays, ASN, agent utilisateur, empreinte JA4, hôte, chemin, règle ou étiquette, avec des données complètes et non échantillonnées sur 21 jours sans frais supplémentaires. Il coexiste avec le tableau de bord existant de chaque ACL web.
articles.title: AWS WAF launches new Security Analytics Dashboard for real-time investigations

articles.excerpt: AWS Marketplace search, Agent Mode, and AWS sales teams use listings to recommend partner offerings to AWS customers. Partners who sell software and services can now create and improve their listings in AWS Partner Central with the new AI-assisted listing experience. It drafts content from a partner's website and other materials, then shows which sections need clearer details, use cases, or evidence of customer outcomes. For single-AMI products, it also drafts the usage instructions buyers see after subscribing. Partners see, for each section, whether it meets what buyers look for, and choose which suggestions to use and review all content before publishing. Partners can position products and professional services as distinct solutions for different industries, use cases, or outcomes. Each solution gets its own AWS Marketplace page, bringing its case studies and AWS Specializations together with the listing's pricing, reviews, and trust information, so buyers can evaluate and buy from the same page. Buyers can filter search results by Specialization. Partners not ready to share public pricing can publish without it using leads-only listings, through which interested customers request a private offer that reaches the partner as a lead in AWS Partner Central. Partners can test metering and billing setup before publishing, and ask the assistant metering questions while integrating. These capabilities are available now to AWS Marketplace partners in all AWS Regions, except the…
articles.summary: AWS Partner Central propose désormais une expérience de création de fiches assistée par IA pour les produits, services et solutions du Marketplace. L'outil rédige un premier jet à partir du site web du partenaire, signale les sections à préciser et permet de tester la configuration de mesure et de facturation avant publication. Chaque solution obtient sa propre page Marketplace avec études de cas, Specializations, prix et avis, et les fiches sans prix public peuvent recevoir des demandes d'offres privées.
articles.title: AWS Partner Central now supports AI-assisted listing experience for product, services, and solutions

articles.excerpt: Aurora PostgreSQL databases created with express configuration can now move into an Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) with a single API call or a modify action in the Amazon RDS console. This helps you take AI-built prototypes and other applications to production without migrating data, while meeting your security and compliance requirements. You can also create a new database cluster inside a VPC using express configuration. With express configuration, Aurora PostgreSQL lets you create and query a serverless database in seconds. Connectivity runs through an internet access gateway, which makes this a good fit for rapid prototyping and AI agent-driven development. When your application is ready for production, a single ModifyDBCluster API call moves the cluster into a VPC and turns off the internet access gateway. That gives you security groups, private subnets, and features such as Aurora Global Database, Amazon RDS Blue/Green Deployments, and Amazon RDS Proxy. The move requires no data migration, keeps your cluster endpoint the same, and interrupts connectivity only briefly. You can also reverse it with the same API call. This feature is available in all AWS Regions where Aurora PostgreSQL with express configuration is available. To get started, use the Amazon RDS console , AWS CLI, or AWS SDKs. To learn more, see the Aurora User Guide .
articles.summary: Les bases Aurora PostgreSQL créées avec la configuration express peuvent désormais être déplacées dans un Amazon VPC, par un seul appel d'API ModifyDBCluster ou une modification dans la console RDS, sans migration de données et avec un endpoint de cluster inchangé. Ce passage donne accès aux groupes de sécurité, aux sous-réseaux privés et à des fonctionnalités comme Aurora Global Database, Blue/Green Deployments et RDS Proxy. La fonctionnalité est disponible dans toutes les régions où la configuration express est offerte.
articles.title: Aurora PostgreSQL with express configuration now supports Amazon VPC

articles.excerpt: Aurora PostgreSQL and Aurora MySQL clusters can now move from one Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) to another without data migration. You can move a cluster with a single API call or a modify action in the Amazon RDS console. This lets you move a cluster to a VPC with more IP address space or a non-overlapping CIDR range, consolidate your network architecture, or meet changing security and compliance requirements. Previously, moving an Aurora cluster to a different VPC meant creating a new cluster in the target VPC, migrating your data, and updating your applications with new connection strings. Now, a single ModifyDBCluster API call moves your existing cluster to the new VPC. Your data stays in place, your cluster endpoint stays the same, and connectivity is interrupted only briefly during the move. Before you start, turn off features that are tied to the cluster's current VPC, such as Aurora Global Database, Amazon RDS Proxy, and Amazon RDS Blue/Green Deployments. You can set them up again in the new VPC after the move. This feature is available for Aurora PostgreSQL and Aurora MySQL in all AWS Regions where Aurora PostgreSQL with express configuration is available. To get started, use the Amazon RDS console , AWS CLI, or AWS SDKs. To learn more, see the Aurora User Guide .
articles.group_summary: AWS permet de déplacer des clusters Aurora vers un autre VPC par un seul appel ModifyDBCluster, sans migration de données. Les bases Aurora PostgreSQL à configuration express peuvent aussi passer dans un VPC.
articles.group_title: Aurora : déplacement de clusters vers un VPC
articles.summary: Les clusters Aurora PostgreSQL et Aurora MySQL peuvent désormais être déplacés d'un VPC Amazon à un autre sans migration de données, via un seul appel d'API ModifyDBCluster ou une modification dans la console Amazon RDS. Le point de terminaison du cluster reste identique et la coupure de connectivité est brève ; il faut toutefois désactiver au préalable des fonctions liées au VPC actuel, comme Aurora Global Database, RDS Proxy et les déploiements Blue/Green.
articles.title: Amazon Aurora now supports moving clusters to a different VPC

articles.excerpt: Amazon MSK Connect (Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka Connect) now supports restarting both existing and newly created connectors and their tasks in place, enabling fast recovery for streaming data pipelines. Amazon MSK Connect is a fully managed service that allows you to deploy, monitor, and scale Apache Kafka Connect connectors with Amazon MSK (Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka). Previously, recovering from failures required deleting and recreating the connector, resulting in downtime and operational overhead. With this feature, you can restart your connector and all its tasks in place, or selectively restart only the failed tasks, making recovery seamless. You can also restart connectors that have no failed tasks to recover from transient issues or to pick up changes in external systems or dependencies. This restart capability is available at no additional cost through the Amazon MSK Console, AWS CLI, AWS SDK, and AWS CDK in all AWS Regions where Amazon MSK Connect is available. To learn more, visit the Amazon MSK Connect documentation . To get started, visit the Amazon MSK Console .
articles.summary: Amazon MSK Connect permet désormais de redémarrer sur place les connecteurs existants et nouvellement créés, ainsi que leurs tâches, pour une reprise rapide des pipelines de données en continu. Il est possible de redémarrer le connecteur complet ou seulement les tâches en échec, y compris pour des connecteurs sans tâche défaillante. Cette fonctionnalité est offerte sans frais supplémentaires dans toutes les régions où le service est disponible.
articles.title: Amazon MSK Connect now supports restarting existing connectors

articles.excerpt: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime instances now support nested virtualization, so your agents can run their own virtual machines and emulators inside a session with Kernel-based Virtual Machine (KVM). Runtime instances run your agents on Amazon EC2 instances while AgentCore handles provisioning, patching, scaling, and lifecycle management. Nested virtualization serves agents that rely on tools that run in a virtual machine, such as mobile emulators or virtual machine sandboxes. You turn on nested virtualization when you create a Linux capacity provider, and agents in every session on its instances can use KVM. For example, your agents can run Android emulators to build and test mobile apps, or start lightweight virtual machines to isolate the code that they run. Nested virtualization works on supported Intel-based instance types, including the C7i, C8i, M7i, M8i, R7i, and R8i families. Nested virtualization is available on supported instance types in all AWS Regions where AgentCore runtime instances are available. To get started, see the following resources: Run virtual machines in agents on runtime instances in the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Developer Guide AgentCore pricing
articles.title: AgentCore runtime instances now support Nested Virtualization

articles.excerpt: AWS Revenue Measurement (previously Partner Revenue Measurement) provides measurement of AWS consumption driven by Partner solutions. Today, AWS announces Identity Tagging in AWS Revenue Measurement, a new way for Partners to get attributed revenue visibility for the AWS usage their solutions drive. Partners can now tag the IAM user or role their solution uses instead of tagging individual resources or decorating individual SDK/API calls. This makes attribution simpler and needs no code changes. Until now, Partners using Resource Tagging had to apply tags to each resource their solution created or managed. That could be hard to keep consistent across customer environments. With Identity Tagging, Partners apply a tag to the IAM role or user their solution uses in the AWS account. AWS Revenue Measurement then attributes usage from resources created by that identity to the Partner's product. Identity Tagging works alongside existing methods such as Resource Tagging, User Agent string, and SaaS Account Tagging, so Partners can pick the method that best fits their architecture. AWS Revenue Measurement is generally available in all commercial regions. To learn more, review the AWS Revenue Measurement onboarding guide .
articles.title: AWS Revenue Measurement now supports Identity Tagging

articles.excerpt: AWS Revenue Measurement (previously Partner Revenue Measurement) provides measurement of AWS consumption driven by Partner solutions. Today, AWS announces expanded Amazon Bedrock support in AWS Revenue Measurement. Partners can now gain attributed revenue visibility for their solutions' use of closed-source models in Amazon Bedrock, giving them a more complete view of the revenue their solutions drive. Until now, only Amazon models (such as Amazon Nova) and open-weight models in Amazon Bedrock were included in AWS Revenue Measurement. With this update, attributed revenue for Amazon Bedrock reflects the total Bedrock charges, including closed-source model usage. Partners who already use Resource Tagging, User Agent string, Identity Tagging, or SaaS Account Tagging for Amazon Bedrock automatically benefit from the expanded coverage, with no additional implementation needed. AWS Revenue Measurement is generally available in all commercial regions. To learn more, review the Amazon Bedrock best practices in the AWS Revenue Measurement onboarding guide.
articles.title: AWS Revenue Measurement now supports closed-source models in Amazon Bedrock

articles.excerpt: Developers on Amazon WorkSpaces Personal can now turn on Nested Virtualization for their own WorkSpaces from the Windows WorkSpaces client, without asking an administrator to make each change. Once an administrator grants self-service permission for the directory, developers can run Docker Desktop, Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL2), and Android emulators directly on their WorkSpaces. Administrators can now grant a directory-level self-service permission for Nested Virtualization. Once granted, end users can turn the setting on or off for their own Windows WorkSpace from the WorkSpaces client. Administrators keep control because the permission is set per directory. Self-service is supported on WorkSpaces Personal, using the Desktop Cloud Visualization (DCV) protocol, on Standard bundles and higher. Power (4 vCPU) or higher is recommended. Value and Graphics bundles are not supported. Nested virtualization is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon WorkSpaces is available, excluding the China (Ningxia) Region. There is no additional charge for supported bundles. For more information, visit the Amazon WorkSpaces documentation on Nested Virtualization . For pricing, visit the Amazon WorkSpaces pricing page .
articles.title: Amazon WorkSpaces now lets developers enable Nested Virtualization

articles.excerpt: Today, AWS Marketplace announces the general availability of Data as a Service, a new product type that lets customers buy third-party datasets and licensed content. Customers often have the models and compute they need, but buying third-party data means adding each provider as a new supplier, negotiating separate contracts, and waiting on procurement cycles. Customers can now find and subscribe to Data as a Service products from AWS Marketplace sellers, and use them to enrich artificial intelligence (AI) applications, analytics, and other workloads. Customers purchase Data as a Service products through public or private offers, and charges appear on their existing AWS invoice. For example, an investment team evaluating private companies can connect its AI agents to private-market data through an API and to credit analysis through a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. Sellers set their own prices and license terms, using a contract, pay-as-you-go, or contract with consumption pricing model for each product. They can add a free trial to any of these models, or offer a product for free. They also define the onboarding and delivery experience, from setting up the customer's account to providing the data through an API, a web portal, a real-time feed, an Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) bucket, or another approach. To learn more, explore Data as a Service products on AWS Marketplace, the AWS Marketplace Buyer Guide , and the AWS Marketplace Seller Guide .
articles.title: Announcing Data as a Service for AWS Marketplace

articles.excerpt: Today, AWS announces that AWS Partner Central Agents now guide AWS Partners to create and enrich opportunities for a high-quality submission, and explain the assigned co-sell motion of each opportunity and why AWS assigned it. Since the launch of Agentic co-selling on June 16, 2026, AWS Partner Central Agents score every opportunity with an Opportunity Quality Score and assign co-sell motions including AWS Field-engaged, Agent-engaged, or Partner-led. When partners create an opportunity, the agents now guide them to a high-quality submission by asking for the details the Opportunity Quality Score measures, such as the customer's business problem, dated next steps, the Partner Primary Need from AWS, and the AWS services the customer will adopt, based on the co-selling best-practice guidance . After submission, the agents explain the reason behind each opportunity's co-sell motion and why AWS assigned it. Where the partner can act, the agents recommend the next step: for Agent-engaged opportunities, how to raise the Opportunity Quality Score; for Partner-led opportunities where AWS co-sell support was not requested, how to progress using agents. As partners act on these recommendations, the score and motion recalculate, and Agent-engaged opportunities move closer to AWS Field-engaged. The new enhanced experience is available today to AWS Partners in the US East (N. Virginia) Region. Partners can also use the agentic experience in native AI tools like AWS Quick and Kiro, or…
articles.title: AWS Partner Central Agents now guide higher-quality co-sell submissions and explain co-sell motions

articles.excerpt: Today, AWS announces AWS Marketplace Express Checkout , a simpler way for businesses that don't have an existing AWS account to buy software from established vendors in AWS Marketplace . Express Checkout is built for businesses that don't use AWS today and just want to buy software. With no cloud setup required, buyers sign in with an email address or a social login, pay with a credit or debit card, and check out in a few steps. Businesses that buy multiple applications this way can manage all of their Express Checkout subscriptions in one place, without a separate billing login for each vendor. From there, they can update their card, download invoices, or cancel a subscription themselves. For sellers, Express Checkout opens a new segment of self-serve business buyers, using the same listing and AWS Marketplace integration they use today. Sellers with an eligible public SaaS listing can request to add their product to the Express Checkout catalog. Express Checkout is available for eligible SaaS products to buyers in the United States and Canada. Businesses that already use AWS can continue to buy in AWS Marketplace with their AWS account. To get started, visit the AWS Marketplace Express Checkout page . To learn more, see the AWS Marketplace Buyer Guide and the AWS Marketplace Seller Guide .
articles.title: AWS Marketplace now offers Express Checkout for buyers without an AWS account

articles.excerpt: Amazon Aurora DSQL now supports PL/pgSQL, enabling developers to create and execute stored functions and procedures directly in the database. Amazon Aurora DSQL is a serverless, distributed SQL database designed for applications requiring active-active availability across multiple AWS Regions with fast reads and writes. You can now encapsulate procedural programming constructs such as IF/ELSE statements, loops, and variable assignments alongside SQL operations within the database. PL/pgSQL support reduces network round trips and improves application performance for data validation workflows, complex calculations, and transactional operations requiring multiple steps. Financial applications can implement account transfer procedures that validate balances, update multiple tables, and handle error conditions within a single database function. PL/pgSQL support is available in all AWS Regions where Aurora DSQL is available. To learn more, see PL/pgSQL in the Aurora DSQL User Guide.
articles.title: Amazon Aurora DSQL now supports PL/pgSQL functions and procedures

articles.excerpt: AWS announces the expansion of the Amazon Connect Customer Competency to Software Partners. The AWS Specialization now recognizes both Services and Software Partners with technical depth and proven success on Amazon Connect Customer—from migrating legacy contact centers and operationalizing AI at scale, to building new solutions on top of Amazon Connect Customer. Modern customers want smooth, tailored interactions wherever they engage, but legacy customer experience systems weren't designed to provide them. They rely on queues, manual routing, and handle-time metrics as control mechanisms, with AI added as a separate layer rather than built in from the start. The Competency adds three new categories for Software Partners: Customer Experience – Solution Extensions , for solutions that integrate with Amazon Connect Customer across the customer experience lifecycle; Connect A2A Collaboration – Agent Certification , for third-party AI agents certified to work alongside Amazon Connect Customer native AI agents during live customer contacts; and Connect Customer – Powered Partner Platform , for Partner-owned solutions that include Amazon Connect Customer as a core component. These join the two existing categories for Services Partners: Contact Center Transformation and AI-Powered Customer Experience. As the first AWS Competency directly aligned to an AWS service, it gives customers confidence they're working with Partners validated by AWS experts to deliver AI-native customer…
articles.title: AWS expands Amazon Connect Customer Competency to Software Partners

articles.excerpt: Customers can now use Amazon EC2 performance status checks and new utilization metrics for EC2 Detailed Monitoring to observe and act on the performance of their EC2 workloads without setup within the instance, complementing their in-guest tooling. Customers running performance-sensitive EC2 workloads can use these signals to monitor their CPU and GPU resources, tune capacity needs, and troubleshoot application issues. EC2 performance status checks identify nonterminal hardware conditions that impact performance on accelerated computing instances. These checks also recommend an action, such as rebooting to complete GPU memory row remapping without replacing the instance. The additions to Detailed Monitoring include support for OpenTelemetry metrics, one-minute GPU metrics that help teams tune accelerated workloads, and a new, higher resolution 10-second CPU utilization metric that helps customers size and scale compute capacity using EC2 Auto Scaling. Customers can selectively opt into these new metrics using categories that they can easily apply to their instances across their fleet. Together, these new capabilities make it easier for customers to manage their compute resources. EC2 performance status checks are available at no additional charge. EC2 Detailed Monitoring metrics are opt-in and incur standard CloudWatch charges for EC2 Detailed Monitoring. These capabilities are available in all commercial AWS Regions and the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. To learn more, see EC2…
articles.title: Amazon EC2 launches performance status checks and new utilization metrics for EC2 Detailed Monitoring

articles.excerpt: Today, AWS announces the Open Data and Interoperability category within the AWS Data Competency. The new category recognizes AWS Software Partners whose solutions keep customer data open and under customer control, letting multiple analytics engines and AI agents work on a single shared copy without moving or duplicating data. AI agents need current, governed data they can reach. According to Gartner, Inc., most organizations are prioritizing AI-ready data investments, yet many Chief Data and Analytics Officers report their current data architecture needs modernization. Partners in the Open Data and Interoperability category are validated for the following capabilities: - Open formats: Data stored in Apache Iceberg, readable by any tool. - Interoperable storage: One copy of data on AWS. - Bidirectional catalogs: Metadata synced through the Iceberg REST Catalog. - Interchangeable engines: Customers pick the right engine for each job. AWS Data Competency Partners also earn performance-based benefits including additional marketing and deal funding in 2027 and access to the AWS Data and AI Workshop. Customers now have a trusted way to find Software Partners whose solutions are built from the ground up for openness and interoperability, and those Partners gain a clear way to stand out. To learn more, read the APN Blog or visit the AWS Data Competency page .
articles.title: AWS Data Competency adds Open Data and Interoperability category for Software Partners

articles.excerpt: AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) announces GetScopedCredentials, a new API that lets you scope down the permissions of existing temporary security credentials. With GetScopedCredentials, you can give your agents, sub agents and workloads their own set of credentials with only the permissions they need. You can call GetScopedCredentials with the temporary security credentials you already use to reduce permissions, session duration, or both. The resulting credentials preserve the caller's original identity, and permissions and session duration are monotonically narrowed so they never exceed those of the caller. Access to the API is controlled with IAM policies, and each call is logged to AWS CloudTrail for traceability. These capabilities make it easier to scope down permissions at runtime without changing how you manage identities. GetScopedCredentials is available in all AWS commercial Regions, AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) Regions and China Regions. To get started, see the GetScopedCredentials API reference and Permissions for GetScopedCredentials .
articles.title: AWS STS announces GetScopedCredentials to scope down permissions at runtime

articles.excerpt: AWS Continuum for Penetration Testing (formerly AWS Security Agent) now lets you pause a running penetration test job and resume it later from its last saved checkpoint. Continuum for Penetration Testing runs on-demand, AI-driven penetration tests against your web applications and APIs. Previously, a pen test job that failed due to client configuration error could not continue, so security teams had to start a new pen test job and repeat work the agent had already done. When you resume a paused or failed pen test job, it keeps its findings and completed work and continues where it left off. You can pause a pen test job during a deployment or maintenance window, raise the task-hour limit of a pen test job that has reached it, or replace test credentials that expired mid-test. Before you resume, you can also update the network traffic settings or VPC configuration, while the pen test job's scope, including its target endpoints, stays the same. You can pause and resume pen test jobs in the web application or with the StopPentestJob and ResumePentestJob APIs. You can resume a pen test job within 7 days of its creation. Pause and resume is available in all AWS Regions where AWS Continuum for Penetration Testing is available. To learn more, visit our documentation page .
articles.title: AWS Continuum for Penetration Testing now supports pause and resume

articles.excerpt: AWS Site-to-Site VPN now supports post-quantum key exchanges to help improve the security posture of your VPN tunnels. This feature supports your migration to post-quantum cryptography based on NIST guidelines. AWS Site-to-Site VPN is a fully managed service that creates an encrypted connection between your data center or branch office and your AWS resources using IPsec tunnels. With AWS Site-to-Site VPN, you can now configure post-quantum key exchange methods in your VPN tunnel options using the CreateVpnConnection and ModifyVpnTunnelOptions APIs. There is no additional charge for using post-quantum key exchanges. This capability is available in all AWS commercial Regions and AWS GovCloud (US) Regions where AWS Site-to-Site VPN is available. To learn more, visit the AWS Site-to-Site VPN documentation .
articles.title: AWS Site-to-Site VPN now supports post-quantum key exchanges

articles.excerpt: Second-generation AWS Outposts racks are now supported in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) Region. Outposts racks extend AWS infrastructure, AWS services, APIs, and tools to virtually any on-premises data center or colocation space for a truly consistent hybrid experience. Organizations of every size, from startups to enterprises to public sector agencies, can now order Outposts racks connected to this newly supported Region to optimize for latency and data residency needs. This regional expansion provides additional flexibility in the number of AWS Regions that customers' Outposts can connect to. To learn more about second-generation Outposts racks, read the AWS Outposts blog post and user guide . For the latest list of countries and territories and the AWS Regions where second-generation Outposts racks are supported, see the AWS Outposts FAQs page . For pricing information in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) Region, please refer to this page .
articles.title: Second-generation AWS Outposts racks now supported in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) Region

articles.excerpt: AWS Health now supports resource and account tags in Health events. This new capability enables you to enrich Health events with resource tags and account tags, providing additional context to help you manage and respond to events more effectively. With this feature, you can now view resource tags directly within Health events for supported AWS services. This allows you to quickly identify which resources are affected and understand their business context without needing to navigate to individual service consoles. Additionally, account-level tags help you categorize and filter events across your organization, making it easier to route notifications and automate responses based on your organizational structure. This enhancement is particularly valuable for organizations managing large-scale AWS deployments. By leveraging tags in Health events, you can streamline incident response workflows, improve cost allocation tracking for health-related events, and enable more granular event filtering in AWS Health Dashboard and AWS Health API responses. The feature integrates seamlessly with Amazon EventBridge, allowing you to create event-driven automation that responds to tagged resources and accounts. This enables sophisticated routing and handling of Health events based on tag values, supporting use cases such as automatically creating tickets in your IT service management system or sending targeted notifications to specific teams. To enable tag enrichment, visit the AWS Health…
articles.title: AWS Health now supports resource and account tags

articles.excerpt: AWS Revenue Measurement (previously Partner Revenue Measurement) provides measurement of AWS consumption driven by Partner solutions. Today, AWS announces Account Tagging for SaaS Products for AWS Revenue Measurement. Partners can now measure the AWS revenue impact of their SaaS solutions by tagging the AWS accounts that host them, instead of tagging individual resources. Until now, Partners with SaaS listings measured that impact through Resource Tagging, User Agent strings, or AWS Marketplace Metering. With Account Tagging for SaaS products, a Partner uses AWS Organizations to tag partner-owned member accounts dedicated to a single SaaS product. The tag key is aws-apn-id-<partner-central-aws-account-id> and the tag value is pc:<AWS Marketplace product-code>. AWS Revenue Measurement then attributes all eligible AWS consumption in each tagged account to that product. Account Tagging for SaaS Products is available for products with a SaaS listing on AWS Marketplace. Each tagged account must be dedicated to one product. Partners whose products share an account can continue to use Resource Tagging, User Agent string, or Identity Tagging. AWS Revenue Measurement is generally available in all commercial regions. To learn more about implementing AWS Revenue Measurement, review the onboarding guide for more information.
articles.title: AWS Revenue Measurement now supports Account Tagging for SaaS Products

articles.excerpt: AWS License Manager now supports AWS Managed Microsoft AD (Hybrid Edition) , so you can use your existing Microsoft Active Directory (AD) to manage user-based subscriptions for Microsoft Office, Visual Studio, and Remote Desktop Services Subscriber Access License (RDS SAL). Hybrid Edition, a feature of AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory, extends your existing directory into AWS. License Manager now works with that directory directly, so you no longer need to bear the cost of duplicating and maintaining the directory in AWS for licensing. Previously, onboarding Microsoft user-based subscriptions required a trust relationship between your directory and a second directory in AWS. If your security policies didn't allow that trust, you couldn't onboard without changing those policies. Now, license-included Microsoft Office and Visual Studio instances that you launch on Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) join your existing directory and apply the same Group Policy settings, such as security baselines and audit policies, so you don't need to recreate them in a second directory. This feature is available in all AWS Regions where AWS License Manager user-based subscriptions and AWS Managed Microsoft AD (Hybrid Edition) are available. To learn more, see the AWS License Manager User Guide , or get started in the AWS License Manager console .
articles.title: AWS License Manager now supports AWS Managed Microsoft AD (Hybrid Edition)

articles.excerpt: Amazon Connect Customer now provides agents with a generative AI-powered post-contact summary of each chat conversation inside the Contact Control Panel (CCP) within seconds after the chat ends, so agents can complete after contact work from the summary instead of rereading the transcript. The summary covers what the customer needed, the actions the agent took, and any open items, and it appears at the end of the chat transcript. Conversational analytics already generates these summaries for voice and email contacts in the CCP, and this launch adds chat. An airline agent who finishes a flight rebooking chat sees the new travel date, the fare difference charged, and the confirmation sent, then writes the wrap-up note from those three facts. Summaries follow your flow's redaction settings and use the same security profile permissions as voice summaries, so administrators who already enabled voice summaries can turn on chat analytics with post-contact summary in the Set recording and analytics behavior block. To learn more, see View generative AI-powered post-contact summaries in Connect Customer .
articles.title: Amazon Connect Customer now provides AI chat summaries in the CCP

articles.excerpt: Today, we are excited to announce the general availability of voice cloning in Amazon Polly, as a gated release. Using a few minutes of recordings from a consenting speaker, you can now create a cloned voice that sounds like that speaker. The cloned voices run on the Amazon Polly Generative engine, which delivers similar naturalness and accuracy as the rest of the generative voices. Voice cloning launches in seven languages: English, Spanish, German, French, Italian, Portuguese, and Hindi. Each cloned voice speaks the language it was recorded in. The cloned voices are automatically encrypted and access-controlled: only you can access your cloned voices. Amazon Polly is a managed service that turns text into natural-sounding speech. With voice cloning, you can give your brand one recognizable voice across IVR and contact centers, voice agents, mobile apps, advertising, and connected devices. You can also create multiple voices for content creation use cases such as audiobooks, e-learning, podcasts, videos, and game characters. Amazon Polly does not retain a copy of your voice recordings once the voice is created and doesn't use them to train Polly models. Voice cloning is available in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (Zurich), Europe (London), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Canada (Central), and AWS GovCloud (US-West).
